title: BT Glucose Meters and Initial Calibration problems
body:
Hi. 
I am still really struggling with initial calibrations and the Contour Next One (likely the same for other BT meters). 
When ever you do a finger prick on the Contour Next One, and you have xDrip set to use Auto Calibration, if you are on the screen to enter your intial calibration, it overwrites that with the normal calibration prompt. Is there a way that when you are doing an initial calibration, xDrip doesn't get distracted by using the BT meter for normal calibration points? Just ignore the meter during these times, so when you are on the screen to enter the intial calibration, it doesnt jump out of it or do something stupid thinking that the system is already up and running... Or possibly even have xDrip fill in the first Initial Calibration spot with the received value, rather than changing screens away from the initial calibration screen.
On the initial calibration screen, and do the finger prick, and up pops 'do you want to use this as a calibration point' like normal, closing the initial calibration screen (or hiding it at least). Select yes, and it doesn't think its an initial calibration point, yet puts it on the calibration graph anyway. Select no, and from memory you have to go back into the initial calibration screen again.

comments.body:
> @WanaGo Would you please close this issue if it has already been resolved?
> Otherwise, would you please update?
> Thanks

Hi.
Its exactly the same as per the initial message.

What exactly happens if you say yes when you say it doesn't think it's an initial calibration?

What CGM do you use?

If you say yes, it just puts a square BG value on the unpopulated graph (as you have no data on there yet), it does not go into the initial calibration screen. The Square point never turns into a calibration as you have no data around it to validate it as being a valid calibration value for the Auto Calibration.

Dexcom G5.
Do you use native or non-native mode?  These may be irrelevant to the bug.  But, others may ask the same question.

Non-native, standard xdrip mode etc.
Its not just limited to the Contour Next One meter either, other BT meters do the same thing, its about how xDrip handles BT readings coming in while its on the initial calibration screen.

> @WanaGo My understanding of automatic calibration is that when you perform a blood glucose measurement, with your Bluetooth meter, it's reading after being transferred to xDrip is used for calibration if the trend is flat enough.
> 
> If that is the idea behind automatic calibration, you should never use a calibration menu.
> 
> What happens if the next time when the initial calibration form pops up and asks for calibrations, you respond by dismissing the form and then performing a blood glucose measurement. Does it not use the reading as a calibration?

Hi again
Not sure we are talking about the same thing here. 
I am talking about a new sensor, waiting for it to warm up, saying its ready and looking for initial calibration values (very first values from finger prick), you do the finger prick and the BT sends it to the xDrip, and instead of inserting the value into xDrip for the initial (FIRST) calibration to start the whole process off, it cancels the initial calibration screen and records it like any normal blood reading.
The trend being flat enough I dont think is relevant as there is no trend, it has no calibrations up to this point, it has no plot, it has no calibration graph or any calibration values set, its a new sensor.

For an existing sensor, finger prick, BT sends to xDrip, it puts the square dot on the trend and it will use it if its in line with whatever parameters it bases the calibration on - that all works fine.
I am talking about the first ever calibration of a new sensor here.

You are correct.  Thanks for pointing that out.
In that case, you can tap on the square marker and tap on calibrate and confirm that you want to use the point as a calibration.
Please try this the next time.
And that is the same as doing an initial calibration from the menu, is it?

The values coming from a glucose meter, by default, are only entered as blood glucose readings, not calibrations.  In order to use one as calibration, one has to tap on it and choose to use it as calibration.

Enabling automatic calibration is supposed to use the incoming readings as calibrations if some conditions are met.  However, as you mentioned, those conditions are not met before initial calibrations are entered.  

Therefore, I am thinking, one should be able to manually, as I described, tell xDrip to use the reading as a calibration.
We can reopen this if needed.
